issue.title: Raise the sase-core-rs floor to >=0.34.63 and admit smoke_sase_core_rs_tool_runs to the release-core-floor job
issue.description:
Epic sase-135 landed 14 `tool_run_*` bindings that `sase` now hard-depends on, but `pyproject.toml` still declares `sase-core-rs>=0.34.48,<0.35.0`. Those bindings first appear in sase-core `44b82c3`, which release `v0.34.63` contains — so unlike the earlier beads of this shape, the containing release already exists; only the declared floor and the CI smoke list lag.

`just check`'s advisory core-floor probe reports this today at master `9a56fc1294`:

```
[core-floor-probe] stale_actionable: sase-core-rs==0.34.48 is missing 21 capability(s) that exist in a published sase-core release.
[core-floor-probe] tool_run_begin: first appears in sase-core 44b82c3 ...; release v0.34.63 contains it.
```

(14 of the 21 named capabilities are `tool_run_*`; the rest belong to earlier cohorts.)

Two things remain, in order:

1. Raise the floor to `>=0.34.63` through `tools/ratchet_core_window`. The release workflow already runs this during "Reconcile release metadata" in `.github/workflows/publish.yml`, so this may land on its own at the next sase release — confirm rather than assume.
2. Add `tools/smoke_sase_core_rs_tool_runs` to the release-core-floor smoke list in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (alongside `smoke_sase_core_rs_telemetry`, `..._at_reference_file_gate`, `..._bead_resolution`, `..._feature_flag_state`, `..._plan_header`, `..._glossary_line_break`). The epic's plan requires the release workflow to run the new smoke once its floor contains the contract, and phase 1 explicitly deferred it because no containing release existed then. The smoke exists and runs today against the local build via `just smoke-tool-runs` (Justfile line 335); only the published-floor job is missing it.

Step 2 must not land before step 1, or the floor smoke will fail against a 0.34.48 wheel that has no `tool_run_*` exports.

This is non-blocking for local and dev gates — the probe is advisory and dev installs build sase-core from the pinned `sase-core-revision.txt` revision — but a PyPI install of sase that resolves `sase-core-rs==0.34.48` pairs the shipped `sase tool` command with a binding that has no ToolRun ledger at all.

Proposed by phase bead sase-135.1 (epic sase-135) as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note, whose stated precondition ("do not add tool_run_* to published-floor REQUIRED_BINDINGS until a containing sase-core release exists") is now satisfied by v0.34.63; filed by the sase-135 land agent on 2026-09-20.

task_type_fields.impact: A PyPI install of sase that resolves the declared floor sase-core-rs==0.34.48 gets a binding with no ToolRun support, so every sase tool list/run/runs/show invocation fails on a missing binding. Local and dev gates are unaffected because they build sase-core from the pinned revision and the probe is advisory.
task_type_fields.repro: At master 9a56fc1294 run: .venv/bin/python tools/probe_core_floor --advisory --sase-core-dir sase/repos/linked/sase-core (this is the step 'just check' runs after 'SASE validation'). It reports status stale_actionable and names tool_run_begin, tool_run_finish, tool_run_list, tool_run_show, tool_run_reconcile, tool_run_append_event, tool_run_summary, tool_run_store_stats, tool_run_normalize_definition, tool_run_canonicalize_fingerprint, tool_run_unknown_evidence, tool_run_retention_apply, tool_run_retention_preview and tool_run_wire_schema_version as first appearing in 44b82c3 / release v0.34.63.

The later af6b1f475 only touches tools/probe_core_floor and does not affect that job.
